about: The code-behind suite of council_core.llm_bench. Each case is a small generated app (its ports: name, kind, type, starting value), the button whose handler the model writes, what that button must do, and a HIDDEN test the model never sees. The test runs in a fresh interpreter against council_core.bench_ports stand-ins with: app (the window; app.errors lists report_error calls), P (app.ports; port.value is the raw widget state a user would have typed, port.items()/rows() the list/table contents), clock (the fake time, when fake_clock is set), tmp (a scratch folder), num(text) (first number in a text) and norm(text) (lower-cased, spaces collapsed). 'linked' names Council modules the handler may import (the app is then a linked project).

cases.name: Sum two numbers
cases.task: When the Add button is pressed, show the sum of First number and Second number in the result label. If either box is blank or not a number, show the text 'Invalid input' in the result label instead.
test: assert num(P.result.value) == 6.5, '2.5 + 4 should show 6.5; the label shows %r' % P.result.value
assert num(P.result.value) == 999.0, '-1 + 1e3 should show 999; the label shows %r' % P.result.value
assert 'invalid input' in norm(P.result.value), 'a blank box should show Invalid input; the label shows %r' % P.result.value
assert 'invalid input' in norm(P.result.value), "'abc' should show Invalid input; the label shows %r" % P.result.value

cases.name: Filter a list
cases.task: When Filter is pressed, show in the fruits list only the items of the ORIGINAL list (the items it held before the first filter) whose text contains the search text, ignoring upper/lower case and keeping their order. An empty search shows every original item again. Also show how many items are now shown in the count label, e.g. '3 items'.
test: assert P.fruits.items() == ['Apple', 'apricot', 'Grape', 'Pineapple'], "'ap' should leave Apple, apricot, Grape, Pineapple; the list holds %r" % P.fruits.items()
assert num(P.count.value) == 4, 'the count label should say 4; it shows %r' % P.count.value
assert P.fruits.items() == ['Banana'], "'AN' must search the ORIGINAL list, ignoring case; the list holds %r" % P.fruits.items()
assert P.fruits.items() == ORIGINAL, 'an empty search should restore every original item; the list holds %r' % P.fruits.items()
assert num(P.count.value) == 6, 'the count label should say 6; it shows %r' % P.count.value

cases.name: Load a CSV into a table
cases.task: When Load is pressed, read the CSV file whose path is in csv_file. Its first row is the header; put every following row into the table (each row as a list of its values) and show 'Loaded N rows' in the status label, N being the number of data rows. If the file cannot be read, call self.report_error('Load CSV', exc) with the exception and empty the table.
test: assert rows == [['bracket', '4', 'Ti-6Al-4V'], ['lug', '12', '316L'], ['plate, thin', '1', 'IN718']], 'the table should hold the 3 data rows (a quoted comma included); it holds %r' % rows
assert num(P.status.value) == 3, 'status should say Loaded 3 rows; it shows %r' % P.status.value
assert not app.errors, 'a readable file reported an error: %r' % app.errors
assert app.errors, 'a missing file must be reported with self.report_error'
assert P.table.rows() == [], 'the table must be emptied when the file cannot be read; it holds %r' % P.table.rows()

cases.name: Image statistics
cases.task: When Analyze is pressed, call image_stats.image_pixel_stats(path) on the path in image_path. It returns a dict with the keys 'width', 'height' and 'brightness' (a float), or a dict with an 'error' key when it fails. Show the brightness rounded to 1 decimal in the brightness label (e.g. '127.5') and the size as 'W x H' (e.g. '640 x 480') in the size label. On failure, call self.report_error('Analyze', the error text) and clear both labels.
test: assert num(P.brightness.value) == 100.0, 'a flat grey 100 image should show brightness 100.0; the label shows %r' % P.brightness.value
assert norm(P.size.value).replace(' ', '') == '40x20', 'size should show 40 x 20; the label shows %r' % P.size.value
assert app.errors, 'a failed analysis must be reported with self.report_error'
assert P.brightness.value == '' and P.size.value == '', 'both labels must be cleared on failure; they show %r and %r' % (P.brightness.value, P.size.value)

cases.name: Validate an email
cases.task: When Check is pressed, decide whether the text in email is a valid address: exactly one '@'; at least one character before it; after it a domain that contains a '.', where the domain does not start or end with '.'. Ignore spaces at either end of the text. Show exactly 'Valid email' or 'Invalid email' in the message label.
test: for text, ok in [('ann@example.com', True), ('  bob@mail.co.uk ', True), ('ann.example.com', False), ('ann@example', False), ('@example.com', False), ('ann@@example.com', False), ('ann@.com', False), ('ann@example.com.', False), ('', False)]:
want = 'valid email' if ok else 'invalid email'
assert norm(P.message.value) == want, '%r should give %r; the label shows %r' % (text, want, P.message.value)

cases.name: Toggle a stopwatch
cases.task: The Start / Stop button toggles a stopwatch. A press while stopped starts timing and shows 'Running' in the state label. A press while running stops it, shows 'Stopped' in the state label, and shows the seconds since the start press in the elapsed label with one decimal followed by ' s' (e.g. '2.5 s'). A later press starts a new timing from zero. Read the time with time.monotonic().
test: assert norm(P.state.value) == 'running', 'the first press should show Running; state shows %r' % P.state.value
assert norm(P.state.value) == 'stopped', 'the second press should show Stopped; state shows %r' % P.state.value
assert norm(P.elapsed.value) == '2.5 s', 'elapsed should show 2.5 s; it shows %r' % P.elapsed.value
assert norm(P.state.value) == 'running', 'a third press should start again; state shows %r' % P.state.value
assert norm(P.elapsed.value) == '1.0 s', 'the new timing should start from zero (1.0 s); elapsed shows %r' % P.elapsed.value

cases.name: Save entries to JSON
cases.task: When Save is pressed, write the JSON object {"name": <the name text>, "age": <the age as an integer>, "subscribed": <true or false>} to the file whose path is in output_file, and show 'Saved' in the status label. If age is blank or not a whole number, write nothing and show 'Age must be a whole number' in the status label.
test: P.name.value = 'Ada'; P.age.value = '36'; P.subscribed.value = True; P.output_file.value = str(out)
assert out.exists(), 'Save wrote no file at the output path'
assert data == {'name': 'Ada', 'age': 36, 'subscribed': True}, 'the file should hold name/age/subscribed; it holds %r' % (data,)
assert norm(P.status.value) == 'saved', 'status should show Saved; it shows %r' % P.status.value
assert not out2.exists(), 'a file was written although age is not a whole number'
assert 'whole number' in norm(P.status.value), 'status should say Age must be a whole number; it shows %r' % P.status.value

cases.name: Convert units
cases.task: When Convert is pressed, convert the number in amount from the unit chosen in from_unit to the unit chosen in to_unit (the units are mm, cm, m and in; 1 in = 25.4 mm). Show the result with exactly 3 decimals, a space and the target unit, e.g. '2.540 cm'. If amount is blank or not a number, show 'Enter a number' in the result label.
test: P.amount.value = v; P.from_unit.value = a; P.to_unit.value = b
assert norm(P.result.value) == want, '%s %s -> %s should show %r; the label shows %r' % (v, a, b, want, P.result.value)
assert norm(P.result.value) == 'enter a number', "'x' should show Enter a number; the label shows %r" % P.result.value
